title: Finite Q3 Euclidean two-slice tail-moment bridge
question: Can the finite Q3 tail fourth leg be identified with a beta/2 Euclidean two-slice correlation and bounded by an equal-time fourth moment without assuming Gibbs commutation?

mathematical_interface.quarter_root: For normalized rho, set S=rho^(1/4) and R=rho^(1/2).
mathematical_interface.tail_moment: For self-adjoint W, ||S W||_4^4 = Tr(R W^2 R W^2).
mathematical_interface.euclidean_two_slice: Tr(R W^2 R W^2) = Z^(-1) Tr(exp(-beta H/2) W^2 exp(-beta H/2) W^2), the beta/2 Euclidean two-slice correlation of W^2.
mathematical_interface.spectral_form: In an H eigenbasis the same quantity is sum_ij sqrt(p_i p_j) |(W^2)_ij|^2.
mathematical_interface.coercive_envelope: The arithmetic-geometric mean inequality gives 0 <= two_slice <= Tr(rho W^4) <= ||W||_infinity^4 for every finite self-adjoint W.
mathematical_interface.qft_role: This is the finite OS/KMS-facing insertion needed by the direct Duhamel lane; it does not supply a source/volume/cutoff-uniform local moment or a common infinite-volume dynamics.
